changes: Default-off --p2p and live host setting; explicit cooperative file download action, ordinary native downloads retained
Browser WebRTC DataChannels with no external STUN/TURN; bounded host discovery, acknowledged signaling queues, leases and file-version-isolated membership
Portable project-owned C++ SHA-256, on-demand 16-piece digest pages, 1 MiB transfer pieces verified before output, corrupt/missing/offline peer fallback to pinned HTTP Range
Bounded chunk cache, four connections and 4096 KiB/s aggregate upload per page by default, 120 seconds of post-download sharing, explicit stop and pagehide cleanup
Disk-backed streaming and verified existing-file resume where local write APIs exist; bounded Blob fallback for small files; pause/cancel/error commit and exponentially spaced COW checkpoints
TCP-IP/cookie/key/access-revision binding and existing token/Origin/login/hotlink guards; idle control polling does not extend hotlink access
No new third-party dependency; compressed embedded assets and ES5 syntax maintained

P2P authenticated join and hotlink expiry despite periodic idle polls
Existing HTTP core/Server/backpressure suite with 5 GiB offset and 144 mixed Range operations
Access/login/five-attempt ban/manual unlock/strict host/COW copy/hotlink/QR/gzip regression
Full HTTPS regression: TLS1.2/1.3, ALPN/resumption/close-notify, trust/SAN/RSA/ECDSA/DER, 96 concurrent ranges, streaming/chunked upload/gzip, preview/MCP/key aliases and handshake budgets

verification.macos: Source-compatible portable code only; no build or test per user instruction

limits: Remote LAN P2P requires a trusted secure context; ordinary insecure IP HTTP and IE use existing native downloads
Native save-file picker and large-file COW behavior are covered by test doubles only; no actual picker or multi-GB/TiB endurance run
Actual WebRTC proof uses two loopback pages, not separate physical LAN machines or production-scale concurrent peers
One cooperative download per page; nonempty regular/native-mounted files only, maximum1TiB; active browser materialization is excluded
No external STUN/TURN; blocked UDP, network isolation and absent peers can eliminate bandwidth savings
First copy usually still needs host data and on-demand hashing adds disk reads; no throughput/savings guarantee
COW checkpoints are spaced to reduce repeated copying, not a zero-copy persistence guarantee; crashes can lose uncommitted progress and disk APIs may need extra space
Client-reported aggregate peer bytes are advisory, not trusted billing or exact host traffic accounting
Received content cannot be revoked; custom malicious clients are not constrained by the webpage stop button
